name: Moped
description: A two-wheeled motor vehicle, with or without pedals, whose electric motor produces less than 2,000 watts and can propel it past 20 mph on its own or keeps assisting a pedaling rider past 28 mph.

restrictions.rule: Two tandem wheels, either of them at least 10 inches in diameter; pedals are optional
Its electric motor produces less than 2,000 watts and can propel it faster than 20 mph by itself, or keeps assisting past 28 mph while the rider pedals; an electric bicycle is never a moped
restrictions.citation: Delaware Code Title 21 §101(40), as amended by House Substitute 1 for HB 439

restrictions.rule: A moped is a motor vehicle rather than a bicycle, and an electric two-wheeler of 2,000 watts or more is a motorcycle
Riders need a driver's license, carried while riding, but no motorcycle endorsement; a nonresident needs a valid license from their home state
Riders and passengers under 18 must wear a fastened helmet meeting the bicycle helmet standard
Titled and registered with the DMV for $5 per three years, with a moped plate on the rear; registrations expire December 31
Exempt from safety inspection, but the DMV verifies the VIN of one first titled in another state
Barred from interstate and limited-access highways, even to cross them, and from railroad rights-of-way except to cross
Barred from bike lanes, sidewalks and any pathway closed to motor vehicle traffic
restrictions.citation: Delaware Code Title 21 §4198M, as amended by House Substitute 1 for HB 439

restrictions.rule: Bicycle traffic rules apply to it on public roads
restrictions.citation: Delaware Code Title 21 §4198M, as amended by House Substitute 1 for HB 439

restrictions.rule: Sellers may not sell, rent or lease it as an e-bike or labeled Class 1, 2 or 3, or advertise it as legal on a public pathway or bike lane; every ad must disclose its legal class, motor power in watts and brake horsepower, top speed, and that registration, license and insurance rules apply and insurance might not cover it, and the buyer signs a written disclosure of the same before the sale, which the seller keeps for 3 years; a violation is an unlawful practice under the Consumer Fraud Act
restrictions.citation: Delaware Code Title 21 §8701, added by House Substitute 1 for HB 439
